affirmations.text: What happened to me was not my fault. I am reclaiming my sense of safety one day at a time, and my healing journey deserves patience and respect
My past does not dictate my future as a mother or as a woman. I am safe in this moment.
This craving is temporary. I have the strength to weather this storm.
Higher Power, grant me the patience to be the gentle mother my children need today.
I can speak to myself with kindness while I learn a different way to live.
I do not have to be a perfect mother to offer my children love, attention, and repair.
I can pause before I respond. A small moment of quiet can help me choose my next step.
Higher Power, help me receive support instead of carrying every burden alone.
I am allowed to set boundaries that protect my recovery, my rest, and my dignity.
I can tell a trusted person when I am struggling. Asking for support is part of caring for myself.
My feelings deserve to be heard. I can share them at a pace that respects my boundaries.
I can notice one small kindness today without pretending that everything is easy.
When I make a mistake, I can take responsibility, apologize, and practice a more caring response.
Higher Power, guide my words toward gentleness and help me listen to my children with care.
Rest does not have to be earned through exhaustion. My needs matter, too.
I can focus on the next manageable choice rather than solve my whole future today.
I deserve support without shame. I can choose people who respect my healing.
I can recognize what is within my control and let that guide where I place my energy today.
Healing has its own pace. A difficult day does not erase the care I have given myself.
Higher Power, help me meet uncertainty with patience and accept the help available to me.
Small moments of connection count. I can offer my children my attention without having every answer.
I can say no to what overwhelms me and yes to what supports my recovery.
I can appreciate a step forward without comparing my journey to anyone else’s.
An urge is a feeling I can name. I can pause, use my recovery tools, and reach out for support.
Higher Power, remind me that caring for myself can help me show up with more patience and love.
I am more than my hardest chapter. My worth does not depend on a flawless day.
I can choose how much of my story to share. My experiences do not belong to everyone.
I can make room for both my children’s feelings and my own, with care and appropriate support.
Today I can make space for a breath, a boundary, and one act of kindness toward myself.
Higher Power, help me honor the steps I have taken and approach tomorrow with hope and humility.
